addressed.problem: `add` accepts an empty participants list. The expense is stored, and every later `balances()` call raises ValueError from `split(cents, 0)`. One bad `add` makes the whole ledger unusable, which breaks the rule that a failed `add` changes nothing and that validation happens before any state change.
addressed.evidence: ledger.py:36-43: `names = []` passes `all(names)` (True for an empty list) and the empty set passes the duplicate check. The expense is appended at line 44. In `balances`, `split(expense.cents, len(expense.participants))` is called with 0 (line ~58) and money.py:23 raises ValueError. `Ledger().add('2026-01-01','Ann','1.00',[])` succeeds, then `balances()` raises.
addressed.fix: In `add`, before building the Expense, raise ValueError if `not names` (for example `if not payer or not names or not all(names)`).
addressed.if_skipped: A caller who passes an empty participant list silently corrupts the ledger. `balances()` and `settle` then fail for every period that includes that expense, and the only way out is to discard the Ledger.

plan: Baseline: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` passed (34 tests) and `python3 -m unittest discover -s acceptance` passed (17 tests).
Contracts: ledger to money/dates and settle to ledger balances, tested from the consumer's side in `qa/test_qa.py`.

Integration: 200 random expenses go through Ledger.balances and then settle. Balances sum to 0, there are at most n-1 transfers, and every balance ends at 0. Period balances also sum to 0 for each month from months_between.

Edge cases: parse_amount rejects `1.`, `.5`, `+1`, `1e2`, Arabic-Indic digits and `-`. parse_date rejects trailing newline, leading space, year 0000 and full-width digits. split sums and mirrors for many cent and part values. A failed Ledger.add leaves balances unchanged. settle leaves its input unchanged.
Acceptance: AC-001 to AC-017 are already covered in `acceptance/`, so I did not duplicate them.
Regression and non-functional: discarded. There was no code before this architecture, and the architecture names no security or performance requirements.
All 9 QA tests pass. None were left red on purpose. The test named `test_d1_*` checks that an empty participant list is rejected. It passes and is not a defect.
gaps: Dates near `datetime.date.max` (for example month_end(9999-12-31)) raise OverflowError instead of ValueError. Section 6 doesn't specify this, so I didn't report it as a defect.
Section 6 doesn't say what an empty `participants` list should do. The code raises ValueError, which is reasonable.
Python 3.9 compatibility was not run, because only the local interpreter was available.
Rerun command from the repo root: `python3 -m unittest discover -s qa -p 'test_qa.py'`.
